 Summary
 AMD stock slipped 0.17% to $503.41 on November 17, 2026, a smaller loss than the Nasdaq Composite's 0.74% drop.
 None of the reports reviewed named a company-specific cause; filings showed an executive's plan-based share sale and Appaloosa's full exit from AMD.
 Nvidia reported after the close, and Yahoo Finance said AMD was among the chip stocks that rose in post-market trading.
 Table of Contents Gotrade News - In the latest AMD stock news, Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) stock slipped 0.17% to close at $503.41 on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, a smaller loss than the Nasdaq Composite's 0.74% drop. 
 None of the reports reviewed for this article tied the dip to company news; it came on a day when all three major US indices fell, and the session closed before Nvidia reported earnings.

 How AMD Traded in the Session
 AMD opened at $512.12, which was also the session high, then slid as low as $480.50 before recovering to close $22.91 above that low. Volume reached 36.3 million shares, 18.60% above the 30.6 million-share average.
 The stock held up better than the broad market. The Nasdaq Composite fell 0.74% to 24,328.38, the S&P 500 dropped 1.03% to 7,340.53 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 1.64% to 50,759.42, while the 10-year Treasury yield eased 2.0 basis points to 5.10%. That left AMD 0.57 percentage points ahead of the Nasdaq.
 Read also: Gotrade Daily: Anthropic Debut and Walmart Results Tonight Chip peers were mixed. Nvidia (NVDA) slipped 0.44% to $155.46 ahead of its report, Broadcom (AVGO) rose 2.46% to $341.60 and TSMC (TSM) fell 3.68% to $359.69. At the close, AMD sat 23.55% below its 52-week high of $658.52 and 167.46% above its 52-week low of $188.22.
 Why AMD Stock Fell
 None of the reports reviewed for this article names a company-specific cause for the 0.17% decline, which was milder than the losses in the major indices. Three dated items framed the session.
 According to a Form 4 filing listed on AMD's investor relations site on November 17, executive vice president and general manager Forrest Norrod sold 10,000 shares on November 16 at weighted average prices between $503.40 and $508.20. The filing says the sales were made under a Rule 10b5-1 trading plan he adopted on May 20, 2026.
 As reported by 24/7 Wall St. , David Tepper's Appaloosa sold all 197,500 of its AMD shares in the quarter ended September 30, according to a 13F filed on November 16. The filing does not say why the fund sold.
 The regular session ended before Nvidia's third-quarter results . Per Yahoo Finance , Nvidia beat Wall Street's expectations and reiterated its long-term forecast after the close, and AMD was among the chip stocks that rose in post-market trading.
 AMD Stock Analysis: Supporting Factors and Risks
 Supporting Factors
 Revenue growth: AMD's third-quarter revenue rose 44.7% to $13.38 billion, as reported by 24/7 Wall St.
 Read-across from Nvidia: Nvidia's results beat expectations and it reiterated its long-term forecast, which Morningstar analyst Brian Colello called "really encouraging," per Yahoo Finance.
 Risks
 Sector volatility: Yahoo Finance reported that the semiconductor trade has been volatile since Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO, with investors questioning the succession plan.
 Disclosed selling: Norrod's plan-based sale and Appaloosa's full exit were both filed this week, and the Appaloosa filing does not give a reason.
 Wide swings: the stock moved between $480.50 and $512.12 in one session and remains 23.55% below its 52-week high.
